clue.text: Where second-hand sellers are quick to pocket a bit of cash

indicators.note: to pocket is to enclose, so the word for quick goes round the cash phrase

parts.note: fleet means quick, swift of foot
the mark was the German unit of currency, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Dealers in used goods are always swift to slip some money into their pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' looks like part of the definition's description of sellers, but it is the outer word; mark is the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market of stalls is where secondhand goods and bric-a-brac are sold cheaply.

clue.text: Foreign aid originally given to nervous Moslem dynast

indicators.note: originally points at the opening letters of foreign and aid

parts.note: timid means nervous, shy

explanation.surface: Overseas help first went to an anxious Islamic ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives F and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fatimids were an Islamic dynasty ruling North Africa and Egypt; one ruler of that line.

clue.text: See discomfited person eat his words, set up artificially?

indicators.note: discomfited means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch an embarrassed man having to eat his words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discomfited' rearranges PERSON EAT; the definition describes a constructed language.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is a language invented by Zamenhof, a vocabulary made up artificially.

clue.text: Concern shown after thousands caught by currency fiddle

indicators.note: shown after places the concern word behind the first part
caught by means held inside, so the thousands letter goes within the currency word

parts.note: currency is money
K stands for a thousand
a concern is a business, a firm

explanation.surface: Worry about large sums tied up in a currency scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry in the surface but means a firm; K for thousands is a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business means trickery or shady dealing, a swindle.

clue.text: Plant producing paper with a lot of quality

parts.note: a rag is a newspaper of low quality

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the quality word loses its last letter

parts.note: worth is quality or merit

explanation.surface: A factory turns out paper of considerable quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts the H from WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Paints about fifty English VIPs

indicators.note: about means around, so the VIPs word goes round the fifty

parts.note: names are famous people, big names
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: An artist portrays around fifty important English figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside NAMES; E goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamel is to coat with a glossy paint, so the verb means applies such coating.

clue.text: Twisting fellow heading for criminal record

indicators.note: twisting round means the fellow's name is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a common man's name, standing for any fellow

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, taken here from criminal

explanation.surface: A crooked man gets himself a criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisting' turns SID into DIS; 'heading for' gives the C of criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat disc carrying recorded sound.

clue.text: First person to criticise organised religion

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to attack institutional faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the faith founded by Muhammad, one of the world's great religions.

clue.text: Scream appropriate, dropping extremely expensive cut glass

parts.note: to cry is to scream

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so a letter is taken out of the appropriate word

parts.note: to appropriate is to steal
the extremes of the word expensive are the letter E at each end, and one E goes

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks at the theft of costly glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes an E, the letter at either extreme of 'expensive', out of the word for appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is high-quality glass, often cut into facets.

clue.text: Question handiwork etc, craftily in pulling a fast one?

indicators.note: craftily means artfully, so the letters of handiwork etc are reworked

explanation.surface: Querying someone's work and so on, slyly, in the course of a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' rearranges HANDIWORK ETC; the definition imagines a gunfighter pulling a gun fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being swift to draw a gun is what a fast gunslinger does; the question mark flags the pun on a trick.

clue.text: Clip recording simple goal

indicators.note: to clip is to cut short, so the last letter of the recording word is trimmed off

parts.note: taping is recording on tape

explanation.surface: A short extract of tape shows an easy goal being scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' trims the final G from TAPING.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a tap-in is a ball nudged into the net from very close range, an easy score.

clue.text: After a drug bust collaborate bit by bit

indicators.note: after tells us the collaborate word follows the rearranged letters
bust means broken up, so the letters of a drug are rearranged

parts.note: to ally is to join forces, collaborate

explanation.surface: Once the narcotics raid is over, people slowly start cooperating with the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a police raid in the surface but signals an anagram making GRADU.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradually means step by step, slowly over time.

clue.text: Means to communicate way to limit high score

indicators.note: to limit is to bound, so the way word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner

indicators.note: high in the sense of drunk or wild, so the letters of score are jumbled

explanation.surface: A method for keeping a scoreline down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' makes RSECO from SCORE; 'high score' looks like a phrase but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The dots-and-dashes telegraph system is a method of sending messages.

clue.text: Launch attack to repel a potential space invader

indicators.note: to repel is to drive away, so the a of the clue is removed from the phrase

parts.note: to come at someone is to launch an attack on them

explanation.surface: An army mounts an offensive to drive off an alien invader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repel' removes one A from COME AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is a celestial body that might, in fantasy, threaten Earth from outer space.

clue.text: Idiot commanding battalion's captured

indicators.note: captured means held within, so the answer sits inside the words commanding battalion

explanation.surface: A fool is in charge, and the battalion has been taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured', with the 's read as 'has', signals letters held inside commanDING BATtalion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbat is slang for a foolish or crazy person.

clue.text: Vacillating Social Democrat finally resigned

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering, so these letters shift into a new order
finally points at the closing letter of Democrat

explanation.surface: A wavering Social Democrat eventually quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the last letter of Democrat; 'Vacillating' rearranges SOCIAL plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned means accepting one's fate patiently, the stoic attitude.

clue.text: Can she go abroad to get married in oriental dress?

indicators.note: abroad means astray or scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Might a woman travel overseas to wed in Eastern costume?
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges CAN SHE GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar.

clue.text: Do well or do badly, almost having to accept defeat

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the shortened word goes round the defeat word
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to bomb is to fail completely
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Someone might either thrive or flop, nearly having to take a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do well' and 'do badly' look like a pair of opposites in the surface; only the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to flourish and develop well.

clue.text: Pick on -rough up — someone making a scene

annotationWithheld.why: Pick on — rough up — someone making a scene (7), BEST BUY: 'Pick' defines it, but no parse of 'on rough up someone making a scene' gives BESTBUY (BEST BOY is a film crew job, yet nothing fairly changes O to U)
annotationWithheld.clue: Pick on -rough up — someone making a scene

clue.text: Be involved in slightly different match play

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so be goes inside the rearranged letters
slightly different means altered, so the letters of match are shuffled

explanation.surface: Get involved in a game played under altered rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly different' makes MACTH from MATCH; 'match play' looks like golf but play is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy.

clue.text: Articles written during depression recalled where miners would meet

indicators.note: written during means put inside, so the articles go within the reversed word
recalled means brought back, so the depression word is read backwards

parts.note: a dip is a depression or hollow
the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Some newspaper pieces composed in a slump remember a mining gathering place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DIP into PID; 'written during' puts THE and A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a mine shaft is where colliery workers gather before going down.

clue.text: Joke's thrust I'll understand in foreign language

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a jab is a quick thrust
the I of I'll

explanation.surface: I'll get the point of the joke in another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understand' is a link: I'll understand the gag, the surface says.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the language of the Punjab in India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Around midnight guy working shows resentment

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the guy word goes round the midnight letter

parts.note: a dude is a guy, a man
G is the middle letter of night, mid-night
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A man on the night shift shows bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle of 'night', G; 'Around' puts DUDE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon means a feeling of offence or indignation, as in high dudgeon.

clue.text: One penned by poet as young lover

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the one goes inside the poet word

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Swan of Avon, so a poet is a swan
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A youthful romantic is someone a poet has written about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts I inside SWAN; Shakespeare was the Swan of Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a country youth or suitor.

clue.text: This isn't still a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail that is anything but quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means moving about, the opposite of motionless.

clue.text: Anxious chap ends affair

parts.note: a concern is a matter or affair
Ed, a man's name for a chap, comes at the end of the answer, which is what ends says

explanation.surface: A worried man breaks off a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' reads as a verb in the surface; it only places the chap after the affair word.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned means worried or troubled.

clue.text: Novel set in city with bishop meeting a biblical character

parts.note: Bath is an English city in Somerset
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A book is set in a cathedral city where a cleric meets a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE is Rider Haggard's adventure novel; BATH is a Somerset city.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament she was the wife of Uriah, taken by King David.

clue.text: Girl's right in front of tree, not behind it

indicators.note: in front of says the right letter must now stand at the head of the tree word
not behind it says that letter leaves its place at the back of the tree word

parts.note: the osier is a willow tree

explanation.surface: A girl is told she is right to stand ahead of the tree, not behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: An osier is a willow; its last letter, R for right, is moved from the back to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a female first name.

clue.text: Reverse heavily-laden vehicle into compound

indicators.note: reverse here means the vehicle word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart, as used by brewers

explanation.surface: A driver backs a heavy truck into an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' turns DRAY backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is an enclosed area beside a building.

clue.text: Miss running meeting daily about one?

indicators.note: about means around, so the cleaner word goes round the one

parts.note: in Britain a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in daily, a charwoman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Does a cleaning woman deal with something every day?
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaner who comes in each day; 'about' puts I inside CHARWOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A female person who presides over a meeting, addressed as Madam, chairs it.
